label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
Here's the post:

---

Last Saturday we wrapped up the Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms (5-7 November, Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune). As one of the three organisers, I'm writing this on behalf of the team to say thank you.

For those who weren't there, a few numbers: 112 applications, 41 participants selected (MSc and early PhD students) on a statement and one reference, coming from 9 states. The school was funded by a Rs 2.4 lakh grant from the institute's student initiative, which covered hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation students.

Our thanks go to:

Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, our faculty mentor, for her guidance from start to finish.

Our speakers: Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad) on Mordell-Weil, Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai) on modular forms, and Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki, who joined online from Kraków for computations in Sage.

The 6 PhD students who worked as TAs and ran the problem sessions. That format worked really well and we will keep it.

Mr. Prakash Salunke from the office, who sorted out our hostel rooms at 11pm when the booking got messed up.

My co-organisers, Ketaki Joglekar and Faizan Mirza.

And all 41 participants, who asked questions, argued at the whiteboard and made the school what it was.

Two moments I'll remember. On day 2 the power went out for nearly two hours in the afternoon and the laptops died. We moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards, and it turned out to be the best session of the three days. And when an MSc student from Silchar spotted an error in a worked example in Sunanda ma'am's notes, she corrected it live and thanked him. That is exactly the kind of exchange a small school makes possible.

I do think small schools like this matter more than big conferences for MSc students, because they actually get to ask questions.

Slides and problem sheets will go up on the department website in about two weeks.

We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, though that depends on whether the grant comes through. If it does, we would love to see many of you back. Thank you all once again.

#EllipticCurves #ModularForms #NumberTheory #WinterSchool

---

It comes to about 370 words and roughly 2,400 characters with spaces, so it's within both limits. If you'd rather leave out the hashtags, it's still over 360 words.

Before you post, check the "in about two weeks" line, since slides were promised by a date you may want to name exactly. Since the post is going out on 11 Nov, you could say "by 25 November" if you're confident about it.
